'''Business and economy'''
*[[France–Niger relations]]
**[[Niger]]'s [[National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland|military junta]] revokes the operating license of [[France|French]] nuclear fuel producer [[Orano]] at the [[Imouraren mine|Imouraren uranium mine]] amid tensions between the two countries. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0kked7ydqyo (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents''' 
*[[2024 Hajj disaster]]
**At least 1,119 [[pilgrim]]s, more than half of whom are from [[Egypt]], are now confirmed to have died from heat-related causes during the [[Hajj]] in [[Saudi Arabia]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/saudi-state-did-not-fail-after-hundreds-dead-during-hajj-official-to-afp-d8c5ff8e (''Barron's'')]
**[[President of Tunisia]] [[Kais Saied]] dismisses the [[Ministry of Religious Affairs (Tunisia)|Minister of Religious Affairs]] after 49 [[Tunisia]]ns are reported to have died in this year's Hajj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/north-africa/2024/06/21/tunisia-sacks-religious-affairs-minister-amid-hajj-casualties (Al Arabiya)]
*[[2024 Guangdong floods]]
**The death toll from the [[flood]]s and [[landslide]]s in [[Meizhou]], [[Guangdong]], [[China]], increases to 47 people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/21/death-toll-from-southern-china-floods-reaches-47 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2024 North America heat waves]]
**At least six people die due to [[Heat illness|heat-related illness]] in the [[Phoenix metropolitan area]] in [[Arizona]], [[United States]], as temperatures reach {{conv|115|F|C}}. [https://apnews.com/article/arizona-heat-deaths-59ddc3afd1052d482b836723ed22e88e (AP)]
*[[2024 West African floods]]
**At least 21 people are killed by floods in Niger's [[Maradi region]] and the suburbs of [[Niamey]] after unusually heavy rainfall in the region. [https://apnews.com/article/niger-floods-rain-rainy-season-climate-change-desert-c7616a35d99a9e831fba69da7a46d5b8 (AP)]
*[[2024 European heatwaves]]
**Most of [[Montenegro]] and parts of [[Albania]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], and [[Croatia]] experience [[Power outage|blackouts]] as a result of a heavy load on the electrical grid caused by an unexpected increase in power consumption due to high temperatures. [https://www.dw.com/en/balkan-countries-suffer-blackouts-amid-major-heatwave/a-69440332 (DW)]
*At least 11 people are killed in wildfires in [[Southeastern Anatolia Region|southeast]] [[Turkey]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/agricultural-fire-spreads-settlements-southeast-turkey-leaving-5-111303409 (ABC News)]
*A worker is killed and five others are critically injured in an explosion at an [[aluminium]] processing plant in [[Bolzano]], [[South Tyrol]], [[Italy]]. [https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/flash/2024/06/23/-esplosione-in-fabbrica-a-bolzano-morto-un-operaio-_a15eb025-390a-4fc6-a53b-709d044a496f.html (''ANSA'')]
*[[France]] reports nearly 200 cases of [[cholera]] in [[Mayotte]]. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2024/06/21/france-reports-almost-200-cholera-cases-in-mayotte_6675367_7.html. (''Le Monde'')]
*The death toll from torrential rains in [[El Salvador]] increases to 19 people, including at least two children. [https://apnews.com/article/el-salvador-san-salvador-rains-landslides-emergency-8275ca07e9669ad629bd5a933e0a2fa3 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Enlargement of the European Union]]
**[[Accession of Moldova to the European Union]], [[Accession of Ukraine to the European Union]]
***[[European Union]] member states agree to begin negotiations on the accession of [[Moldova]] and [[Ukraine]] to the EU next week. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/ukraine-ap-belgium-russia-moldova-b2566648.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[Moldovan president]] [[Maia Sandu]] signs the decree that begins negotiations on Moldova's accession to the European Union. Sandu also announces that the first Moldova–EU intergovernmental conference will take place on 25 June. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/moldovan-president-signs-decree-on-start-of-eu-accession-talks/3254874 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Armenia–Palestine relations]], [[International recognition of the State of Palestine]]
**[[Armenia]] officially recognises the [[State of Palestine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/armenia-recognises-palestinian-statehood-says-armenian-foreign-ministry-2024-06-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Ukraine relations]]
**[[Israel]] and Ukraine mutually impose travel restrictions to each others' citizens, preventing reciprocal visa-free travel without an authorization permit. [https://kyivindependent.com/israel-ukraine-to-suspend-visa-free-regime/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')]

'''Law and crime''' 
*[[2024 Fordyce shooting]]
**Four people are killed and ten others are wounded in a shooting at the Mad Butcher supermarket in [[Fordyce, Arkansas]], United States. The suspect, Travis Eugene Posey, is shot and arrested by [[Arkansas State Police]]. [https://apnews.com/article/arkansas-grocery-shooting-a4c8496ca2fc60feb1f52e5298cbecc2 (AP)]
*[[Cross-Strait relations]]
**[[China]] officially defines [[Taiwan independence movement|Taiwanese separatist behavior]] as a criminal act. [https://www.ft.com/content/eac10230-8436-4e7e-9999-816797afbd58 (''Financial Times'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Namibia]]
**The [[Judiciary of Namibia|High Court]] of [[Namibia]] rules that two [[German South West Africa|colonial-era]] laws criminalizing [[sex between men]] are unconstitutional. [https://www.dw.com/en/namibia-court-says-laws-banning-gay-sex-unconstitutional/a-69436971 (DW)]
*A court in [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]], sentences [[India|Indian-born]] billionaire [[Prakash Hinduja]] and three of his family members to four years in prison for exploiting domestic workers at their villa in [[Cologny]].
